![Project Banner](assets/banner.png) # Graph Machine Learning & Network Topology for Fraud Ring Detection ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.11-3776AB?style=flat-square&logo=python&logoColor=white) ![NetworkX](https://img.shields.io/badge/NetworkX-3.1-blue?style=flat-square) ![Scikit-Learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-F7931E?style=flat-square&logo=scikit-learn&logoColor=white) ![LightGBM](https://img.shields.io/badge/LightGBM-2E7D32?style=flat-square&logo=lightgbm&logoColor=white) ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green?style=flat-square)

Uncovering financial crime syndicates, money mule funnels, circular layering rings, and collusive transaction networks using graph topological invariants and gradient-boosted decision trees.

--- ## Overview Traditional financial fraud detection systems analyze transactions and accounts as isolated, independent observations. They rely primarily on tabular heuristics such as historical account balance, account age, and single-transaction velocity. Modern financial crime syndicates systematically circumvent these tabular defenses through distributed, multi-account structures: 1. **Money Mule Funnels (Smurfing):** Multiple originator nodes transmit fragmented, sub-threshold balances into intermediate mule accounts, which aggregate the capital before routing it to terminal cash-out exits. 2. **Circular Layering (Wash Trading):** Capital cycles through closed directed loops ($A \to B \to C \to A$) to manufacture fictitious payment histories, generate transaction volume, and obscure criminal origins. 3. **Collusion Rings:** High-frequency, densely connected subgraphs characterized by abnormal internal transaction density and reciprocated fund flows. When evaluated purely on tabular account metrics, individual syndicate participants mimic benign customer behavior. By modeling the banking ecosystem as a directed, weighted multigraph $\mathcal{G} = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E}, \mathcal{W})$, graph machine learning captures non-local connectivity invariants, degree imbalances, centrality concentrations, and community modularity to expose organized syndicates. --- ## Architecture & Methodology
![Pipeline Architecture](assets/pipeline-architecture.png)
The graph fraud detection pipeline operates across six distinct computational phases: 1. **Directed Transaction Graph Ingestion:** Ingests 2,500 banking entities and over 12,000 directed financial transactions, constructing a weighted graph where edge weights capture transaction counts and volumes. 2. **Topological Feature Engineering:** Computes nodal graph invariants including in/out degree ratios, flow volume imbalances, PageRank centrality, ego-network clustering coefficients, and Louvain modularity partitions. 3. **Hybrid Feature Fusion:** Concatenates tabular account metadata with extracted graph structural metrics into a unified feature space. 4. **Dual-Model Benchmarking:** Trains a baseline tabular LightGBM model and a graph-augmented LightGBM model under identical stratified splits and hyperparameter budgets. 5. **Precision-Recall Diagnostic Evaluation:** Benchmarks detection efficiency on an imbalanced syndicate cohort (3.60% positive prevalence), assessing PR-AUC lift and false positive reduction. 6. **Ego-Network Forensic Audit:** Extracts and visualizes sub-graph topologies to provide anti-money laundering (AML) compliance analysts with interpretable evidence packages for regulatory reporting. --- ## Dataset & Graph Topology Schema The dataset comprises 2,500 accounts connected via directed payment interactions with an empirical fraud prevalence of 3.60% (90 confirmed syndicate nodes across three embedded crime typologies). | Feature Attribute | Data Type | Domain Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | account_id | Integer | Unique identifier for bank account node | | account_age_days | Integer | Trailing days elapsed since account opening | | avg_monthly_balance | Float | Mean deposit balance maintained over trailing 12 months ($) | | kyc_risk_score | Float | Initial customer onboarding risk score (0.0 to 1.0) | | in_degree | Integer | Total count of distinct incoming payment counterparties | | out_degree | Integer | Total count of distinct outgoing payment counterparties | | total_degree | Integer | Aggregate degree centrality (in-degree + out-degree) | | degree_ratio | Float | Normalized counterparty flow ratio ((in-degree + 1) / (out-degree + 1)) | | in_tx_amount | Float | Cumulative incoming financial transaction volume ($) | | out_tx_amount | Float | Cumulative outgoing financial transaction volume ($) | | tx_amount_ratio | Float | Capital velocity ratio ((incoming volume + 1) / (outgoing volume + 1)) | | pagerank | Float | Global PageRank centrality score within the transaction network | | clustering_coefficient | Float | Local ego-network transitivity and triadic closure coefficient | | community_id | Integer | Assigned graph modularity cluster partition via Louvain algorithm | | community_size | Integer | Total number of account nodes residing within the assigned community | | is_fraud | Binary Target | Ground truth label: 1 = Confirmed Syndicate Participant, 0 = Legitimate | --- ## Network Topology & Syndicate Visualization Visualizing the transaction network reveals pronounced structural divergence between benign account clusters and tightly coordinated fraud syndicates.
![Graph Network Topology](assets/graph-network-topology.png)
### Structural Observations - **Benign Accounts:** Exhibit scale-free, diffuse connectivity with low local clustering. Transactions distribute sparsely across diverse merchant, payroll, and peer-to-peer endpoints. - **Fraud Syndicate Clusters:** Form abnormally dense subgraphs with high internal connectivity and extreme directional flow imbalances. Syndicate nodes consistently occupy topological anomalies that are invisible when evaluating accounts in isolation. --- ## Ego-Subgraph Audit: Money Mule Funnel Forensic deep-dives into detected syndicates reveal the tripartite architecture of money mule operations.
![Ego-Subgraph Inspection](assets/ego-subgraph-inspection.png)
### Smurfing Funnel Typology 1. **Smurfing Origin Nodes:** Multiple low-balance accounts execute repeated transfers beneath mandatory currency transaction reporting thresholds. 2. **Intermediate Mule Accounts:** Intermediary nodes rapidly aggregate incoming disbursements, exhibiting elevated in-degree metrics and near-zero account retention periods. 3. **Terminal Cash-Out Nodes:** Highly centralized collector nodes that pool aggregated capital and execute rapid external liquidations or wire transfers. --- ## Community Detection & Louvain Modularity Analysis Applying the Louvain modularity optimization algorithm partitions the global network into cohesive sub-communities based purely on transaction density without supervision.
![Community Risk Distribution Heatmap](assets/community-risk-heatmap.png)
### Quantitative Community Risk Profiles | Community ID | Total Accounts | Confirmed Fraud Accounts | Empirical Fraud Density | Modularity Profile | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- | | Community 5 | 58 | 35 | 60.34% | High-density money mule aggregator network | | Community 2 | 27 | 16 | 59.26% | Circular layering ring with dense chord cycles | | Community 4 | 63 | 30 | 47.62% | High-frequency bipartite collusion syndicate | | Community 8 | 188 | 9 | 4.79% | Marginal boundary cluster with peripheral mule overlap | | Baseline Graph | 2,164 | 0 | 0.00% | Benign commercial and retail transaction flows | Syndicate fraud is not uniformly dispersed across the banking graph; instead, over 90% of all fraudulent entities are concentrated within just three detected modular communities. Incorporating community-level risk signals provides strong structural priors for downstream classifiers. --- ## Quantitative Benchmarking & Model Evaluation Given the severe class imbalance (3.60% fraud prevalence), Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC-AUC) can present an overly optimistic assessment due to the vast majority of true negatives. **Precision-Recall AUC (PR-AUC)** serves as the primary metric to accurately evaluate positive class discrimination and operational alert quality.
![Performance Comparison](assets/performance-comparison.png)
### Quantitative Performance Metrics | Evaluation Metric | Tabular Baseline Model | Graph-Augmented Model | Performance Delta | Operational Assessment | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- | | **Precision-Recall AUC (PR-AUC)** | **0.0517** | **0.9960** | **+94.43 pts** | Near-perfect separation of complex syndicate networks | | **ROC-AUC** | **0.5426** | **0.9998** | **+45.72 pts** | Resolves severe false alarm rates of tabular heuristics | | Detection Lift Over Random | 1.4x | 27.7x | +26.3x | Concentrates AML compliance review capacity on true threats | | Input Dimensionality | 3 tabular features | 13 hybrid features | +10 features | Minimal feature overhead with exponential signal gain | The tabular baseline fails completely on syndicate participants, achieving a PR-AUC of 0.0517 (barely above the 0.036 random prevalence baseline). By contrast, the graph-augmented classifier achieves a PR-AUC of 0.9960, capturing structural invariants that tabular models cannot observe. --- ## Topological Feature Importance & Structural Dominance Analyzing split-gain feature attribution demonstrates that structural network invariants overwhelmingly dominate gradient-boosted decision trees when detecting organized financial crime.
![Topological Feature Importance](assets/topological-feature-importance.png)
### Key Structural Drivers - **Degree Ratio & In/Out Flow Imbalances:** Accounts receiving funds from dozens of sources while funneling outward to a single endpoint exhibit extreme degree ratio anomalies, instantly flagging mule aggregators. - **PageRank Centrality:** High PageRank nodes embedded within dense sub-clusters reliably separate cash-out hubs from ordinary commercial merchants. - **Louvain Community Size & Density:** Membership in small, tightly coupled communities provides critical contextual priors that isolate wash-trading rings. - **Tabular Account Baselines:** Features like account age and average balance contribute minimal split gain, confirming that sophisticated syndicates readily manufacture convincing individual account profiles. --- ## License MIT: [LICENSE](LICENSE)
